title: Agriculture, Iron, and the Bantu Peoples

questions.prompt: The word “diffused” in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: emerged
was understood
spread
developed

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 1, why do researchers doubt that agriculture developed independently in Africa?
options: African lakes and rivers already provided enough food for people to survive without agriculture.
The earliest examples of cultivated plants discovered in Africa are native to Asia.
Africa’s native plants are very difficult to domesticate.
African communities were not large enough to support agriculture.

questions.prompt: In paragraph 1, what does the author imply about changes in the African environment during this time period?
options: The climate was becoming milder, allowing for a greater variety of crops to be grown.
Although periods of drying forced people south, they returned once their food supply was secure.
Population growth along rivers and lakes was dramatically decreasing the availability of fish.
A region that had once supported many people was becoming a desert where few could survive.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, camels were important because they
options: were the first domesticated animal to be introduced to Africa
allowed the people of the West African savannahs to carve out large empires
helped African peoples defend themselves against Egyptian invaders
made it cheaper and easier to cross the Sahara

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, which of the following were subjects of rock paintings in the Sahara?
options: Horses and chariots
Sheep and goats
Hyksos invaders from Egypt
Camels and cattle

questions.prompt: What function does paragraph 3 serve in the organization of the passage as a whole?
options: It contrasts the development of iron technology in West Asia and West Africa.
It discusses a non-agricultural contribution to Africa from Asia.
It introduces evidence that a knowledge of copper working reached Africa and Europe at the same time.
It compares the rates at which iron technology developed in different parts of Africa.

questions.prompt: The word “profound” in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: fascinating
far-reaching
necessary
temporary

questions.prompt: The word “ritual” in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: military
physical
ceremonial
permanent

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 4, all of the following were social effects of the new metal technology in Africa EXCEPT:
options: Access to metal tools and weapons created greater social equality.
Metal weapons increased the power of warriors.
Iron tools helped increase the food supply.
Technical knowledge gave religious power to its holders.

questions.prompt: Which of the sentences below best expresses the essential information in the highlighted sentence in the passage? Incorrect choices change the meaning in important ways or leave out essential information.
options: While American iron makers developed the latest furnaces, African iron makers continued using earlier techniques.
Africans produced iron much earlier than Americans, inventing technologically sophisticated heating systems.
Iron making developed earlier in Africa than in the Americas because of the ready availability of carbon and iron ore.
Both Africa and the Americas developed the capacity for making iron early, but African metallurgy developed at a slower rate.

questions.prompt: The word “fleeing” in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: afraid of
displaced by
running away from
responding to

questions.prompt: Paragraph 6 mentions all of the following as possible causes of the “Bantu explosion” EXCEPT
options: superior weapons
better hunting skills
peaceful migration
increased population
